method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Separating paperwork from specimens is correct, but thicker paper and lab drying are filler, and a leaking specimen also needs its own containment/integrity response.
issues: Separating paperwork from specimens is correct, but thicker paper and lab drying are filler, and a leaking specimen also needs its own containment/integrity response.
proposedChanges: Use an intact securely closed container with paperwork in the wrong compartment, or explicitly handle leaking specimen per policy. Compare separate pouch, paper wrapped around container, entire package inside a second bag, and a photocopy attached outside; avoid suggesting a leak is solved solely by moving paper.

items.assessment: Access restriction and trained cleanup are correct; large steps over blood is cartoon wrong.
issues: Access restriction and trained cleanup are correct; large steps over blood is cartoon wrong.
proposedChanges: Compare restricting route and arranging cleanup, placing a warning sign, covering spill with absorbent material while awaiting cleanup, and personally beginning cleanup. Specify worker competence/PPE availability to distinguish immediate access control.

items.assessment: Prompt washing with proportionate exposure assessment is correct, but all alternatives are implausible extremes and the key is uniquely nuanced.
issues: Prompt washing with proportionate exposure assessment is correct, but all alternatives are implausible extremes and the key is uniquely nuanced.
proposedChanges: Compare washing exposed skin, applying alcohol hand rub, contacting occupational health before washing, and inspecting source-client infection status. Explain cleaning priority and assess breaks in skin; avoid implying intact-skin exposure equals need for PEP.

items.assessment: Packaging, sterility information and suitability checks are sound; same-brand-last-year is filler.
issues: Packaging, sterility information and suitability checks are sound; same-brand-last-year is filler.
proposedChanges: Use a concrete sterile-kit label and observed wetness/tear/indicator/expiry cues. Ask which findings require replacement; distinguish a familiar brand or external indicator from actual sterility assurance. Vary correct count/positions.

items.assessment: Resolve newborn identification mismatch is correct, but asking another parent is absurd and core objective overlaps087.
issues: Resolve newborn identification mismatch is correct, but asking another parent is absurd and core objective overlaps087.
proposedChanges: Use a displaced/replaced band process with mother-infant pair and compare checking documented identifiers through approved replacement process, relying on cot card, relying on assigned nurse recognition, and relying on parent recognition. Give enough detail to test newborn-specific verification rather than restated stop-mismatch rule.

items.assessment: Required personal identifiers against records prevent wrong care. Chart-nearest-room is filler.
issues: Required personal identifiers against records prevent wrong care. Chart-nearest-room is filler.
proposedChanges: Replace with asking the person to confirm the name read aloud, or matching procedure time. Keep open-ended identifier verification decisive rather than a vague comprehensive key.

items.assessment: Resolving site uncertainty is correct, but silence-as-consent and after-completion documentation are weak; near-duplicate089.
issues: Resolving site uncertainty is correct, but silence-as-consent and after-completion documentation are weak; near-duplicate089.
proposedChanges: Make a distinct team challenge: surgeon says discrepancy was corrected verbally but the team cannot see corroborating record. Compare repeating verified team pause, relying on surgeon assurance, obtaining family recollection, and using booking list. Preserve elective context and explain shared verification.

items.assessment: Current assessed texture plan must match delivered meal, but quick feeding and family visual choice are implausible.
issues: Current assessed texture plan must match delivered meal, but quick feeding and family visual choice are implausible.
proposedChanges: Compare obtaining prescribed texture, cutting regular food into smaller pieces, thickening accompanying fluid while retaining regular food, and selecting naturally soft items from tray. Explain texture standards and assessed plan; do not imply all modified textures interchangeable.

items.assessment: Route tracing, correct connector and order check are correct; solely makes adapter choice self-disqualifying, and overlap084 is substantial.
issues: Route tracing, correct connector and order check are correct; solely makes adapter choice self-disqualifying, and overlap084 is substantial.
proposedChanges: Use a specific enteral-only connector mismatch after transfer and proposed fixes. Remove solely; explain why a generic adapter defeats route-specific protection. Add another credible technical nonkey and vary correct positions/count.

items.assessment: Moving footplates aside is correct; asking client to jump is cartoon.
issues: Moving footplates aside is correct; asking client to jump is cartoon.
proposedChanges: Compare swinging footplates away, helping client slide feet around them, having helper stabilize chair while standing from plates, and raising seat height. State normal planned transfer ability and brakes already locked.

items.assessment: Replacing worn aid components is correct but leaning harder and using only for longer distances are weak.
issues: Replacing worn aid components is correct but leaning harder and using only for longer distances are weak.
proposedChanges: Compare obtaining safe replacement, adding closer assistance during continued use, limiting use to the room, and applying non-slip tape. Use concise parallel key and explain observed equipment failure persists with supervision.

items.assessment: Current weakness requires safe height and mobility reassessment, but lower-after-standing and staff convenience are implausible.
issues: Current weakness requires safe height and mobility reassessment, but lower-after-standing and staff convenience are implausible.
proposedChanges: Compare restoring safe exit height and checking current transfer, lowering to floor-level position regardless of limb length, using bed alarm at treatment height, and relying on baseline independence. Explain individualized exit mechanics versus a universal lowest setting.

items.assessment: Controlling wet-route access is correct. Moving walking aid away is filler and unchanged access explicitly advertises error.
issues: Controlling wet-route access is correct. Moving walking aid away is filler and unchanged access explicitly advertises error.
proposedChanges: Compare arranging a dry alternate route, escorting slowly through damp route, putting up a warning sign, and providing nonslip footwear. State unstable gait or urgent destination to support coordinated access priority.

items.assessment: Resource shortage alone cannot justify restraint; however all nonkeys contain obvious blanket/visibility/sole-justification cues.
issues: Resource shortage alone cannot justify restraint; however all nonkeys contain obvious blanket/visibility/sole-justification cues.
proposedChanges: Compare escalating staffing and assessing wandering needs, obtaining a restraint order, requesting family agreement, and administering an existing agitation PRN. State no immediate danger and calm purposeful walking; explain authorization alone does not establish clinical necessity.

items.assessment: Ownership, practical competency and tested correction are appropriate, but without-changing phrase reveals the nonkey.
issues: Ownership, practical competency and tested correction are appropriate, but without-changing phrase reveals the nonkey.
proposedChanges: Replace with repeating the drill at the next annual exercise or emailing storage instructions as the completed correction. Ask about evidence of resolution with concrete accessibility/competence observations; vary SATA pattern.

items.assessment: Updating evacuation function is correct, but practising walking during alarm and deleting resident are absurd.
issues: Updating evacuation function is correct, but practising walking during alarm and deleting resident are absurd.
proposedChanges: Compare updating assistance/equipment plan now, adding a routine chart mobility note, notifying usual day-shift nurse, and assigning a wheelchair at the next drill. Explain emergency record must reflect current lift dependence and tested available strategy.

items.assessment: Nonclinical latex balloons remain relevant for severe allergy. Removing them is correct; location, symptom waiting and medical-supply-only assumptions are recognizable exposure misconceptions.
Individual equipment or validated processing is appropriate but same-room sharing is filler.
issues: Individual equipment or validated processing is appropriate but same-room sharing is filler.
proposedChanges: Replace with changing the detachable shaving head between residents while retaining shared body, or wiping casing with disinfectant. Device-specific validated instructions must determine any allowed reprocessing; do not imply surface wiping makes all razors shareable.

items.assessment: Changing contaminated clothing and cleaning skin is correct, but hand rub on fabric is cartoon wrong.
issues: Changing contaminated clothing and cleaning skin is correct, but hand rub on fabric is cartoon wrong.
proposedChanges: Compare changing clothes, spot-cleaning with detergent, wearing a clean gown over affected area, and changing after completing current round. Explain contamination remains until appropriately removed; avoid for-rest-of-shift exaggeration.

items.assessment: Planned movement with source control is appropriate; all-mobility-solely cancellation is an obvious nonkey.
issues: Planned movement with source control is appropriate; all-mobility-solely cancellation is an obvious nonkey.
proposedChanges: Use wound drainage covered and client able to clean hands. Compare actual route/equipment plans, shared recreation timing, and hand-hygiene steps. Avoid universal community-space permission; align with organism-specific/local guidance.

items.assessment: Unfamiliar device without instructions requires actual validated process or alternative. Stronger product, analogous device instructions and donor packaging are plausible shortcuts with clear rationales.
Critical tissue entry requires sterilization; key is source-consistent. Sterile wrapper alone is an implausible professional alternative.
issues: Critical tissue entry requires sterilization; key is source-consistent. Sterile wrapper alone is an implausible professional alternative.
proposedChanges: Compare validated sterilization, high-level disinfection, extended disinfectant immersion, and sterile-water rinse after cleaning. This may be foundation unless procedure context requires classification; label honestly and avoid unsupported processing times.

items.assessment: Demonstration and return demonstration are appropriate, but infection-rate leaflet and strongest household cleaner are filler.
issues: Demonstration and return demonstration are appropriate, but infection-rate leaflet and strongest household cleaner are filler.
proposedChanges: Compare device-specific demonstration/return demonstration, manufacturer handout with verbal acknowledgement, caregiver telephone teaching, and referral to supplier teaching video. State client learning/handling barrier and verify reproducible skill.

items.assessment: Observed competence and client suitability establish readiness. Delivery invoice is filler and key uniquely comprehensive.
issues: Observed competence and client suitability establish readiness. Delivery invoice is filler and key uniquely comprehensive.
proposedChanges: Compare observed transfer using correct technique, staff attendance at an in-service, signed reading acknowledgements, and improved completion time. Include client suitability already assessed in stem if focusing competence; explain observation over attendance.

items.assessment: Failed cycle parameters despite intact wrapping is a concrete sterilization misconception. Withholding, tracing and coordinated correction are appropriate; item tests process failure rather than appearance.

sourceCheckNote: Full item-level reasoning/plausibility review; no new primary-source retrieval claimed in this batch. General IPC source checks from earlier reports support broad principles, not a separate technical verification of every item.
